title.narrative: An Innovative and Multi-sectoral Life Saving Intervention for Conflict Affected Communities in Borno state, Nigeria.

description.narrative: ltpgtFor over a decade, Northeast Nigeria—especially Borno State—has faced a prolonged humanitarian crisis driven by insurgency, armed conflict, and displacement. Maiduguri Metropolitan Council (MMC) and Jere LGAs remain heavily affected, hosting large numbers of displaced persons within overstretched host communities. Despite some security improvements, localized attacks, movement restrictions, and chronic service gaps in GBV, Protection Nutrition persist. Women and girls who face sexual violence, intimate partner violence, exploitation, emotional abuse, and early or forced marriage. Fear of stigma, retaliation, and limited safe reporting mechanisms keeps many GBV incidents unreported, leaving survivors without protection or support.ltbrgtNutrition indicators in Borno remain at emergency levels. Children aged 6–59 months continue to experience malnutrition due to food insecurity, limited dietary diversity, poor IYCF practices, and caregiver stress. Families rely on negative coping strategies such as reduced food intake, child labour, survival sex, and early marriage. ltbrgtCOWACDI will implement an innovative GBV and Nutrition integrated intervention in MMC and Jere. Building on its strong grassroots presence and partnerships with NRC and GIZ, also a strong frontline partner of Protection Sector and committed member of the PSEA network, COWACDI will work through existing community structures, women-led groups, and local authorities to strengthen sustainability and local ownership. A mobile GBV case management team will ensure safe access to services, while community protection committees, women’s associations, youth groups, and local actors will be strengthened for improved coordination. The project will reach 23,149 direct participants over 10 months with a budget of USD 200,000, concentrating on the thematic envelope two 2 (Protection of Vulnerable Groups) of the NHF third standard strategy allocation paper for 2025. ltbrgtCOWACDI will establish Gender Reporting Desks within community and government structures. A community-based paralegal system, developed with FIDA, train local women to support survivors with legal guidance, literacy, and accompaniment to justice mechanisms. Capacity building will target volunteers, community leaders, women-led groups, and security actors on survivor-centred approaches, PFA, SEA mitigation, safe referrals, and GBV risk reduction. Creative prevention will include community theatre, digital storytelling, adolescent innovation circles, encrypted referral support, and male engagement platforms promoting positive masculinity, with GBV principles on confidentiality, including safe access to referral services particularly for child survivors.ltbrgtFor Nutrition, COWACDI will conduct active case finding, door-to-door MUAC screening, and rapid referrals. The project will strengthen local nutrition systems through mother support groups, health facility committees, traditional leaders, and nutrition volunteers. Activities include peer groups, father-led feeding dialogues, and cooking demonstrations using local foods. An innovative women-led Tom Brown production model linked to WGSS will support hygienic production, fortification, packaging, marketing, and nutrition messaging—improving child nutrition and supporting women’s livelihoods. Cross-cutting innovations include mobile nutrition data collection, digital GBV case follow-up, and support groups for mothers and adolescents.ltbrgtThrough a locally led and system-strengthening approach, enhanced safety and wellbeing for women and girls, community-based GBV prevention and response, improve early detection and referral of malnutrition, strengthen IYCF practices, expand access to local nutritious foods, and empower women and adolescents. Joint monitoring will be conducted with Christian Aid and NRC. This initiative positions NHF and COWACDI as leaders in innovative, community-rooted GBV and Nutrition programming in Nigeria.ltbrgtlt/pgt
